findings.claim: A quote pair followed by a space still truncates the value during a CONTINUE round trip.
findings.evidence: The change removes the extra unescape but still accepts a partial string-field match. The matcher treats an escaped quote before the space as the closing delimiter and drops the remaining text before this line runs. The fault control has the same executable edit and returns only the prefix and two quotes. Matching the whole field preserves the suffix. The added tests do not cover a space after the quotes.
findings.scenario: Build `fits.Card('TEST', 'x' * 100 + "'' xxx")` and parse its image with `fits.Card.fromstring(card.image)`. The returned value ends in `''` instead of `'' xxx`.

findings.claim: The new string format makes a later numeric condition fail after a valid integer update.
findings.evidence: The candidate stores the exact carry as 1.0000000000000000000000000000000000000E+38. AttributePath.expr calls cast_value, which parses exponent notation as a float. That float is smaller than the 38-digit comparison operand. The pinned Moto baseline and DynamoDB Local both accepted the condition. The candidate returned ConditionalCheckFailedException. Compare numeric operands without losing precision when the stored value uses exponent notation.
findings.scenario: Store amount as 38 nines, then run ADD amount :one with :one = 1. Run a second update with ConditionExpression amount > :floor, where :floor is the original 38-digit integer. The condition must pass.

findings.claim: The new service-parity test bypasses the file's AWS verification helper.
findings.evidence: The existing test uses pytest.mark.aws_verified and dynamodb_aws_verified(). The new mock_aws decorator and fixed table setup skip the marked AWS CI lane and duplicate table setup. Use the existing marker and helper so the assertions can run against both Moto and AWS.

findings.claim: Make the successful late-row test cross the old deadline before the stop chunk.
findings.evidence: The fixture makes the row visible by event count and yields the later chunks and stop immediately. A version that reads ahead but starts the ten-second deadline at the first missing-row check would still pass this test. Advance a controlled clock past the old bound before delivering stop and retain the existing order and completion assertions.

findings.claim: Report the chunk that first blocks on a missing row, once, before reading ahead. Otherwise the adapter can end a response that is still producing chunks.
findings.evidence: Only the read-ahead path calls onProgress. The outer loop can consume the first text chunk and then wait in close() before yielding any event for it. The adapter resets its reasoning deadline on yielded frames or onProgress. The candidate test at line 60 explicitly expects this frame to go unreported.
findings.scenario: With a 600 ms reasoning deadline and a signed row written at response end, the first two text chunks arrive 400 ms apart after the last thinking delta. The first chunk is withheld without a progress report, so the adapter times out at 600 ms even though no gap between engine chunks exceeded 400 ms.

findings.claim: Give consumption of the next live step event one owner, including the stop transition.
findings.evidence: The normal read at lines 66-68 and the read-ahead path at lines 84-88 both clear pending and start the same row deadline on a stop. One shared consume operation can perform both updates; callers only decide whether to encode or hold the event.

findings.claim: Do not introduce a named request subtype just to forward one callback.
findings.evidence: Only the private stream function takes ServedRequestInput, and it uses the sole added field only to forward progress at line 398. The existing request type plus a callback parameter keeps planning input separate from transport progress without an extra type.

findings.claim: Test expiration with controlled time instead of waiting ten wall-clock seconds in a unit test.
findings.evidence: The 15-second timeout lets the test wait through the real row deadline. The test took 10.02 seconds; a controlled clock can prove the same transient failure in a few polls.

findings.claim: An invalid charset name can raise ValueError before the body is read.
findings.evidence: The header parser decodes RFC 2231 parameters before codec lookup. An embedded NUL then makes lookup raise ValueError, but the constructor only catches LookupError. Normalize rejected codec names to DecodingError at decoder construction, separately from content decoding.
findings.scenario: A loopback server sends Content-Type: application/json; charset*=us-ascii''utf-8%00 and a valid JSON body. Calling iter_json raises ValueError instead of DecodingError.

findings.claim: The general decoder module now owns a separate JSON media-framing subsystem.
findings.evidence: The 271-line JSON addition puts three format-specific parsers and media dispatch into the module that owns Content-Encoding handlers and general byte and text helpers. Only JSONStreamDecoder is used from outside the new section. Keep that entry point and its private framing code together in a dedicated JSON stream module, without adding wrappers or changing response methods.

findings.claim: A JSON decoding error can leave a consumed response and its transport stream open.
findings.evidence: The sync JSON iterator has no response cleanup on error. The async counterpart closes its byte generators at line 1100, but the raw generators only close the response after exhaustion. Both paths left response.is_closed and the underlying stream's closed flag false in a focused probe. Close the response when decoding terminates a started stream.
findings.scenario: Feed application/ndjson a chunk containing an invalid terminated line before the final chunk. Iteration raises DecodingError, but the stream remains open and cannot be iterated again.

findings.claim: Valid values are lost if malformed data arrives in the same chunk.
findings.evidence: All three value decoders return a list only after processing the entire chunk. An error later in the chunk prevents the caller from receiving values the parser already decoded. The probe observed different prefixes for identical bodies split at different positions. Yield values from the parser as it completes them.
findings.scenario:
NDJSON chunks b'123
' and b'!
' yield 123 before DecodingError. The same bytes delivered as b'123
!
' raise without yielding 123. JSON arrays and JSON sequences show the same chunk dependence.

findings.claim: A complete top-level JSON object or string does not yield until EOF.
findings.evidence: The non-array state buffers all remaining text and only parses it in flush. With a complete object in the first chunk, next() requested a second chunk before yielding. Yield the completed value and validate trailing whitespace on subsequent reads.
findings.scenario: An application/json server sends a complete object and then delays EOF while sending only whitespace. The caller waits for EOF instead of receiving the object.

findings.claim: JSON sequence framing buffers an invalid preamble until a separator or EOF.
findings.evidence: decode only validates pieces that end in RS. With no RS, even a known-invalid prefix is retained and the iterator requests more data. The probe with b'not-a-record' confirmed the second read. Discard leading whitespace and validate the first nonwhitespace character before buffering a record.
findings.scenario: A streaming application/json-seq response starts with b'not-a-record' and pauses. The iterator waits despite already having enough information to report the framing error.

findings.claim: The JSON methods validate at construction instead of following the lazy response iterator pattern.
findings.evidence: The new methods create the decoder before returning inner generators, while sibling iter_lines/aiter_lines methods execute their setup on the first iteration. The new tests enforce immediate errors even though the task does not require that timing. Put validation in the generator body so stream and validation errors surface at the same iteration boundary.

findings.claim: The candidate adds an unrelated generated TLS key log to the repository root.
findings.evidence: The new file contains only an OpenSSL/Python key log header. The original SSL configuration test sets SSLKEYLOGFILE to test, and the candidate handoff also calls it an unrelated untracked artifact. Omit it from the delivered patch.

findings.claim: Single Source of Truth: the shared helper requires callers to pass the parent path twice.
findings.evidence: The new array and tuple cast calls and the existing nested-test producers all pass `parentPath` as a copy of `options.path`. The helper then uses the separate copy to build the child path. Derive the child path from the parent options instead of requiring callers to keep two inputs in sync.

findings.claim: A nested condition can cause validation to check a replacement value but still return the unchecked element.
findings.evidence: The old implementation captured the element before calling `resolve()`. The candidate reads `testOptions.value` after `resolve()` exposes that same mutable options object to condition builders. In the probe, the base raised `ValidationError`, while the candidate returned the original nonnumeric string from both an array and a tuple. Capture the element before invoking callbacks.
findings.scenario: Use `number().when([], (_, schema, opts) => { opts.value = 1; return schema; })` for an item and strictly validate `['not a number']`.

findings.claim: Validation after container normalization can report a cast element as its original value.
findings.evidence: The fallback uses the container returned by `super._validate`, which has already cast its elements. With numeric coercion after JSON parsing, the probe saw `originalValue` change from string `"42"` during cast to number `42` during validation. The tuple branch uses the same fallback. Preserve the normalized element before element casting instead of substituting the final value.
findings.scenario: Validate the JSON text `["42"]` with `array().json().of(number().when([], (_, schema, opts) => { record(opts.originalValue); return schema; }))`.

findings.claim: Array and tuple casts can read different values for the item and its original value.
findings.evidence: The caller already reads the element, but the helper reads `parent[k]` and `originalParent[k]` again even when both are the same array. The probe read the slot three times for an array and four for a tuple, compared with one and two at baseline. The callback saw `value: 'first'` and `originalValue: 'later'` before any cast. Reuse the element read for the cast.
findings.scenario: Cast a one-element array whose index-zero getter returns `'first'` on its first read and `'later'` thereafter.

findings.claim: Building a lazy schema rereads the original slot before the selected schema captures its input.
findings.evidence: `Lazy.asNestedTest` now builds full options for resolution, then invokes the selected schema's `asNestedTest`, which builds them again. In the strict-validation probe, the base selected a string schema and validated a string. The candidate made an extra early read and validated a number with that string schema. Use one captured set of nested options for resolution and validation.
findings.scenario: Strictly validate an array whose index-zero getter returns `'first'`, `'first'`, `7`, and `'later'` on successive reads. The lazy builder selects `string()` or `number()` from the value's type.

findings.claim: The cast-and-validation tests record metadata they never read.
findings.evidence: The array test and its tuple counterpart at line 118 assert the metadata inside the callback. Their outer assertions use only the recorded indices, and exact array equality already checks the length. Record just the indices and compare their sequences.

findings.claim: The store exposes mutable rollups, so a caller can invalidate the metric index and silently lose a report.
findings.evidence: append keys the bucket by rollup.metric and stores the original object. read returns those same objects, and readonly Rollup[] does not make Rollup.metric readonly. The reader then rejects the rollup in its old bucket without finding it in its new bucket.
findings.scenario: Drain one latency sample, then assign store.read("latency")[0]!.metric = "duration". The latency bucket still holds the rollup, but reports for both latency and duration return undefined.

findings.claim: The second retention test repeats the preceding test without protecting another behavior.
findings.evidence: Both tests give createReader 60 seconds and check that a rollup ending at 50,000 ms remains at 100,000 ms. The first already checks the exact retained value and separately checks expiry at 70,000 ms.

findings.claim: The sample helper adds a metric parameter that never changes the metric used by any test.
findings.evidence: Each caller omits the parameter or passes its default value, latency. The test named for per-metric publication still exercises only one metric. Use two different metrics in that test or keep the original helper.

findings.claim: The insertion-order comment repeats the two statements immediately below it.
findings.evidence: The next two lines already read store.append(newer) and store.append(older), and the test name explains why that order matters.

findings.claim: The close event and try/finally add synchronization that the one-request test does not need.
findings.evidence: Server waits on the optional event only after it has already handled the request and closed its socket. Removing the event and using the Server context manager alone preserved the test's observed baseline failure and candidate pass.

findings.claim: Give FTS5 literal encoding one owner in the search adapter.
findings.evidence: The new map encloses text in double quotes and doubles embedded quotes. The retained fallback in src/infra/conversation-recall-search.ts:154 independently encodes the same kind of FTS5 literal using a regex. Both paths can share one literal formatter without changing whitespace splitting, OR semantics, or the required rawQuery fallback.

findings.claim: The revised hyphen test does not protect phrase matching in a search request.
findings.evidence: It bypasses buildFtsMatch and supplies a hard-coded MATCH expression. With the test's two rows, Bun SQLite returned the same hit for the new quoted phrase and the old OR expression. Extend the transcript search test with the raw query `feature-flag` and a distractor such as `flag the feature for rollout`, which the OR expression matches but the phrase excludes.

findings.claim: Keyword-only queries still disagree between recall and transcript search. Both callers need the same empty-MATCH behavior.
findings.evidence: The filter removes every word from `AND`. Transcript search short-circuits, but recall sends the empty expression to FTS5. FTS5 rejects it, and recall retries the raw query as a quoted literal and returns a hit. This discrepancy also existed on the baseline.
findings.scenario: Index an in-scope entry saying `normal and later`. Search for `AND` in the transcript and call recall with the same query and scope. Recall returns the entry; transcript search returns no hits.

findings.claim: The empty-result quote assertion does not protect quote escaping. Use an internal double quote plus another query word, with separate entries that must match each alternative.
findings.evidence: Removing quote escaping left all five new expectations passing in the SQLite probe. The only double-quote case expects no matches, and the raw-query fallback returns no matches for that fixture even when the generated MATCH is malformed.

findings.claim: Remove the one-off probe from the delivered diff.
findings.evidence: The diff adds a standalone 37-line script that starts a local Redis server for manual verification. The handoff expressly says the probe is not a deliverable, and the Tcl regression does not depend on it.

findings.claim: The negative sequence-delta row does not test whether trimming preserves the full delta.
findings.evidence: With threshold 3-0, truncating the -4294967296 delta reconstructs 2-4294967296 and 3-4294967296. Redis compares milliseconds first, so both the narrow and wide versions delete two entries and keep the same three. Using 2-0 immediately before a 2-1 threshold would make the assertion depend on the sequence comparison.

findings.claim: Derive source-square selection from rank boundaries instead of listing all 64 absolute offsets.
findings.evidence: Line 11 already separates ranks with `~~`. Lines 12 to 75 encode those same boundaries again by skipping offsets 8 and 9, 18 and 19, and so on. Replacing the fixed offsets with one rank-splitting rule and eight file selectors preserved the exact intermediate rows on 2,816 layouts. It also preserved the exact final text for the required example and all 108 qualification positions.

findings.claim: Separate pawn movement from promotion instead of defining each movement direction twice.
findings.evidence: Lines 141 to 146 repeat each of the three pawn offsets with opposite rank guards. A legal input cannot already contain a white pawn on rank eight, so one rule can promote any white pawn that lands there. Three movement rules plus one rank-eight promotion rule preserved the exact output lists, including 288 queen promotions and 58 promotion captures.

findings.claim: Validated dependency edges keep public handle data that the local graph does not need.
findings.evidence: create_compute rejects foreign IDs before storing the edges. Each stored CellId still carries the same reactor serial, and set_value reaches into its private key to read a local index. Normalize to tagged local indices at creation, keeping the reactor serial only on public handles. The host probe measured 24 bytes per public CellId and 16 bytes per tagged local index.

findings.claim: The callback list makes removal by ID linear.
findings.evidence: Lines 269 to 274 search each entry through the match and shift the remaining entries on removal. A stale ID scans the whole list every time. The task does not promise registration order, so a map keyed by callback ID, as in the reference, avoids both operations and preserves the existing missing-ID error.

findings.claim: An input update scans unrelated compute cells instead of following the affected dependency graph.
findings.evidence: Lines 203 and 207–212 allocate marks and inspect dependencies for every compute cell. Setting an input with no dependents still walks the entire graph. The reference records reverse dependencies when cells are created; use those links to select affected cells while retaining the candidate's topological evaluation and deferred notifications.

findings.claim: Callback registration couples independent reactors through one process-wide atomic counter.
findings.evidence: Both reactor creation and every callback registration call the same allocator, but removal only searches the selected cell's callbacks. A reactor-local sequence paired with the existing reactor serial preserves ID uniqueness and stale-ID rejection without making independent reactors share registration state.

findings.claim: The serial allocator manually implements a checked atomic retry loop that the standard library provides.
findings.evidence: Lines 109–118 load, check for overflow, and retry a weak compare-exchange. A checked atomic update with the same relaxed ordering and failure message replaces the loop. Both the current try_update API and its predecessor fetch_update were probed for the previous-value return and exhaustion behavior.

findings.claim: Unary multiplication changes a boolean result to an integer.
findings.evidence: The host multiplication evaluates its single operand unchanged for booleans. The candidate applies a binary multiply with an initial integer 1, which coerces the boolean to an integer. Direct execution printed True for (display (* #t)); the candidate printed 1.
findings.scenario: Run a file containing (display (* #t)) followed by (newline).

findings.claim: A CRLF-terminated pathname is passed to fopen with a carriage return appended.
findings.evidence: ev-path conses every character other than LF into the pathname. With identical path bytes except for the line ending, the LF case printed 42 and the CRLF case reached the recursion limit without printing 42.
findings.scenario: Pipe an existing .scm pathname followed by CRLF into eval.scm.

findings.claim: The source reader requires persistent copies in a shared, finite temporary-file namespace.
findings.evidence: ev-buffer always creates the next /tmp/eval-x... file, and ev-main closes it without deleting it. Two evaluator launches left three files; a 0600 source became a 0644 scratch copy. With all 250 valid basenames occupied, a valid calculator run exhausted recursion instead of running. The native grader explicitly isolates /tmp to avoid this failure across grades.

findings.claim: An unreadable source causes repeated NUL writes instead of a source-open error.
findings.evidence: Host fopen returns False on open failure and fgetchr(False) returns False, not the -1 that ev-copy treats as EOF. Host fputchr converts False to NUL and the copy continues. A bounded probe wrote an opening parenthesis and 31 NULs before the file size cap stopped it.
findings.scenario: Supply a filename that does not exist while the temporary buffer directory is writable.

findings.claim: An unclosed form at the end of a file suppresses output from earlier valid forms and hides the parse error.
findings.evidence: The candidate requires the complete wrapped program to parse before evaluating any form. fread returns the empty list at EOF with unbalanced parentheses; the original CLI evaluates each parsed form before parsing the next. The candidate printed nothing where the original printed the marker and then the missing-parenthesis diagnostic.
findings.scenario: Put (display "finished") and (newline) before a final unclosed (define form.

findings.claim: An unbound identifier error names an internal sentinel rather than the identifier in the user program.
findings.evidence: ev-cell forces a host lookup of ev-undefined-variable on a miss. Direct execution named missing in both lookup and assignment probes; the candidate named ev-undefined-variable instead.
findings.scenario: Run (display missing) or (set! missing 1) without defining missing.

findings.claim: The evaluator rejects a complete pathname on the final stdin line if no newline follows it.
findings.evidence: ev-path stops only on LF, but getchr calls ord on an empty string at EOF. A probe supplied a complete pathname at EOF; the program printed 42 directly, whereas the candidate reported the ord error without opening the program.
findings.scenario: Pipe a valid pathname with printf '%s' into eval.scm for a program that needs no further stdin.

findings.claim: The differential tests run fixtures in the checkout instead of isolating their working files.
findings.evidence: The new helper sets cwd=ROOT for both executions. The existing 10-advanced-features.scm fixture opens callback-test.txt in write mode, so the test creates or overwrites that file in the checkout. The owning upstream verifier runs direct and interpreted fixtures in separate temporary directories.

findings.claim: The diff includes a generated file that neither the evaluator nor the tests need as input.
findings.evidence: 10-advanced-features.scm creates callback-test.txt and writes this exact line itself. Removing the checked-in artifact does not prevent the fixture from running.

findings.claim: The tokenizer's unknown-tag case does not assert the opening offset named by the test. Check `TemplateError.position` directly, as the parser tests do.
findings.evidence: The assertion checks only the error class. Changing only the invalid-tag branch to report offset 999 left the test green for `x{{#with a}}`, whose opening offset is 1.

findings.claim: An `each` block delegates rendering to the input array's `map` method and result constructor. Iterate the items without depending on either.
findings.evidence: `Array.isArray` accepts arrays with overridden methods and array subclasses. The probe threw with `map: null` and returned `00` with an array subclass that uses `Uint8Array` as its species.
findings.scenario: Render `{{#each items}}[{{name}}]{{/each}}` with `items: Object.assign([{name: "A"}, {name: "B"}], {map: null})`. The valid array should produce `[A][B]`, but render throws.

findings.claim: The public error test checks a message substring instead of the exact `TemplateError.position` field. Catch the exception once and use the direct field assertion already used by the parser tests.
findings.evidence: Bun accepts `toThrow("at position 2")` for a `TemplateError` with position `20`. The preceding assertion at line 173 checks only the error class, so both assertions pass for the wrong offset.

findings.claim: The new exact message check makes both existing substring checks redundant. Retain the exact message, name, and position checks.
findings.evidence: The string asserted at line 32 contains both substrings asserted at lines 30 and 31. Deleting those two checks cannot let a wrong message pass.

findings.claim: Keep `BlockNode` private to the parser. No caller needs a separate named export for it.
findings.evidence: `BlockNode` is used only within `parser.ts`. The renderer imports `parse` and `TemplateNode`, and the parser tests import only `parse`.

findings.claim: The test name calls two literal quote characters a null string.
findings.evidence: The input always contains two quote characters, and the assertion requires both to survive. The neighboring test shows what an actual empty FITS string looks like: CONTINUE  '' / comments. Naming this test for a literal quote pair would distinguish the two cases.

findings.claim: Long card values still lose text when two literal quotes are followed by a space and more text.
findings.evidence: Removing the extra unescape preserves the quote pair, but _split still accepts a prefix match from _strg_comment_RE and appends only the captured string. In the verified CONTINUE segment, the match stops at the escaped quotes and leaves xxx and the closing quote unconsumed. Requiring the match to consume the full segment preserves this value in the reference probe. The added tests never use a suffix that starts with a space.
findings.scenario: Set value to "x" * 100 + "'' xxx" and evaluate Card.fromstring(str(Card("CONFIG", value))).value. The candidate returns "x" * 100 + "''", silently dropping " xxx".

findings.claim: The arithmetic methods define the same DynamoDB decimal policy independently.
findings.evidence: Addition and subtraction each build a separate Context(prec=38). The operators differ, but their precision, exponent limits, and traps belong to one policy. Correcting that policy currently requires editing both branches.

findings.claim: Legacy numeric ADD leaks a Python TypeError instead of a DynamoDB validation error.
findings.evidence: The legacy branch now calls DynamoType.__add__ without the operand-type guard used by AddExecutor. Patched Moto leaked TypeError through Boto3, while DynamoDB Local returned a ClientError with code ValidationException.
findings.scenario: Store amount as a string such as S:"5", then use AttributeUpdates to ADD N:"1" to amount.

findings.claim: The regression cases bypass the file's AWS parity test pattern.
findings.evidence: The existing test uses pytest.mark.aws_verified and dynamodb_aws_verified(), which provides a table in mock and real AWS modes. The new test uses mock_aws and creates its own table, so the real AWS workflow's -m aws_verified selection cannot exercise the new arithmetic cases.

findings.claim: Exercise the real adapter and hosted transport callback instead of recreating their watchdog wiring in the test.
findings.evidence: The test supplies its own callback and manually starts and completes reasoning in lines 135 to 137. It does not call the changed hosted bridge or the Anthropic adapter, so disconnecting the callback at agent-bridge.ts:449 would leave this test unchanged even though held chunks would no longer reset the production deadline.

findings.claim: The stream rejects a valid response if the signed row finishes writing just after the stop chunk. Keep the bounded row wait after stop instead of treating the first miss as final.
findings.evidence: The shipped hook posts each item to Flywheel before yielding it back to the engine. AgentRows exposes only complete newline-terminated rows, and the candidate throws on the first read at stop. A probe using the shipped hook and real file reads reproduced the transient failure; the reference waited and completed. The candidate's filesystem test appends the row before yielding stop, so it does not cover this order.
findings.scenario: A hosted response streams thinking and text. Flywheel receives the stop chunk before the engine completes its signed JSONL row. The candidate fails transient even though the row is readable on the next poll.

findings.claim: Reporting transport progress for immediately forwarded chunks duplicates the adapter's watchdog reset. Report it only for chunks held behind a missing row.
findings.evidence: The hosted bridge receives the Anthropic adapter's onProgress callback, which calls streamLiveness.frame(). The adapter already calls frame() for every emitted Anthropic event. A plain text delta with no pending row therefore causes two deadline state updates instead of one.

findings.claim: The unit test schedules a one-second real timer, above the repository's 30 ms limit. Drive the timeout with a test clock or let the stalled source wait for abort without a timer.
findings.evidence: abortableSleep schedules setTimeout with the supplied delay. AGENTS.md prohibits unit-test timers above 30 ms. The healthy case also depends on real 20 ms sleeps keeping ahead of a real 100 ms deadline.

findings.claim: Fixture setup can leak the temporary directory if the initial file write fails. Use the existing temporaryDirectories helper or put setup inside the cleanup scope.
findings.evidence: The test creates the directory at line 30 and writes its first file at line 34, before entering the try block at line 52. If the write throws, the finally block never runs, and the unit runner rejects leftover temporary entries. The adjacent hosted-agent tests use the repository's directory helper.

findings.claim: The sequence parser treats the preamble as a record and retains it even though it contains no value.
findings.evidence: The record buffer stores every decoded chunk until RS or EOF. With 2 MiB of streamed spaces the peak traced allocation was about 4.2 MB. The same path read two extra chunks before rejecting a known invalid preamble. The preamble only needs to check for whitespace or the first RS as bytes arrive.

findings.claim: A transport close failure replaces the required JSON validation error.
findings.evidence: The sync finally block closes the response while its DecodingError is propagating. The async finally block at line 1095 does the same. Both probes surfaced OSError with the DecodingError only in its exception context.
findings.scenario: A custom transport returns a response with Content-Type text/plain and a stream whose close or aclose raises OSError. JSON iteration raises OSError instead of the required DecodingError.

findings.claim: Async byte iteration loses request attribution when a raw reader fails to open.
findings.evidence: The candidate constructs the raw iterator before entering request_context. The old code invoked the same factory inside request_context. The baseline probe attached the request to ReadError, and the candidate did not.
findings.scenario: A Response subclass implements aiter_raw as a factory for an AsyncIterator and raises httpx.ReadError when it cannot open the reader. Calling aiter_bytes now propagates the error without its request, even though the response has one.

findings.claim: The test matrices rerun every synchronous case under both async backends.
findings.evidence: The five AnyIO test functions cross an asynchronous boolean with AnyIO's asyncio and Trio fixtures. The false branch only calls sync HTTPX methods. The cross product adds 101 duplicate sync case instances, including three skips. The gzip test also repeats its synchronous assertion on both backends.

findings.claim: The decoder rejects BOM-encoded NDJSON that starts with a blank line.
findings.evidence: The code replaces utf-8-sig with utf-8, then line 100 strips the BOM only after the blank-line check. It passes the now-empty line to json.loads rather than skipping it.
findings.scenario: Encode the text '\n1\n' with utf-8-sig and send it as application/ndjson. The detected codec decodes a blank line followed by 1, but the iterator raises DecodingError. An explicit charset=utf-8-sig also fails.

findings.claim: Cancelling async JSON iteration can interrupt stream cleanup and prevent a later close from retrying it.
findings.evidence: The finally block awaits aclose in the cancelled scope. Response.aclose sets is_closed before awaiting the underlying stream's cleanup and skips that cleanup on subsequent calls.
findings.scenario: Cancel an AnyIO task while it waits for a second chunk from a custom AsyncByteStream whose aclose awaits before releasing its resource. On asyncio and Trio, the response reports closed, the resource is not released, and another aclose does nothing.

findings.claim: A call to the wrong sync or async API consumes the response without reading it.
findings.evidence: The raw iterator rejects the incompatible stream before marking it consumed. The new finally block then sets is_stream_consumed and calls the wrong close method, masking the original error. Lines 1094-1095 repeat this pattern asynchronously.
findings.scenario: Call iter_json on a response backed by async content and catch the mode error. A later aiter_json raises StreamConsumed, although no bytes were read. The same failed iter_bytes attempt leaves the response usable.

findings.claim: JSON iteration mislabels errors from the byte producer as malformed response data.
findings.evidence: The ValueError and LookupError handler covers advancement of iter_bytes as well as JSON decoding. The async handler at line 1090 does the same.
findings.scenario: A sync or async content iterator sends the first array element, then raises ValueError because its source fails. The matching byte iterator propagates ValueError, but the JSON iterator raises DecodingError.

findings.claim: The document parser buffers one Python string reference per character rather than retaining spans of decoded chunks.
findings.evidence: The decoder appends each character and joins the list at the value boundary. For a 1 MiB streamed array containing one non-ASCII string, peak traced allocations were 21.2 MB, compared with 5.2 MB for json.loads of the same bytes.

findings.claim: The decoder allocates state for formats it will not parse.
findings.evidence: The media type fixes the mode at construction. NDJSON and JSON-seq never use the allocated JSONDocumentDecoder; the document path returns before using the record buffer or flags.

findings.claim: The child-value regression test does not exercise the cast option change it claims to protect.
findings.evidence: ObjectSchema._cast resolves the field's .when() with the property value before it calls Schema.cast. Both assertions passed without the patch and with only the cast spread order reverted. Use a case that observes the value at the affected cast boundary instead.

findings.claim: Nested validation makes a second copy of an options object that it already owns.
findings.evidence: createNestedOptions returns a fresh object. asNestedTest immediately spreads all its fields into another fresh object before adding strict. Set strict on the first object to keep the caller's options untouched without copying every field twice per element.

findings.claim: Changing callback options can change the value that nested validation checks.
findings.evidence: The patch reads testOptions.value after this.resolve(testOptions) runs user callbacks. The baseline captured the value before resolving and passed that snapshot to _validate. Keep the value subject to validation separate from the mutable callback options.
findings.scenario: In a strict array, use number().min(10).when([], (_, schema, opts) => { opts.value = 20; return schema; }) as the item schema. A probe with an index-0 guard confirmed the candidate accepted [1] and returned [1], but the baseline rejected it.

findings.claim: A container transform can attach another element's original value to the item being cast.
findings.evidence: Array and tuple casting index the raw input using an index from the processed array. That index is not an element identity. Use the pre-child-cast element when a container transform changes the position of items.
findings.scenario: Casting ['', 'keep'] through array().compact().of(item) calls item.when with index 0, value 'keep', and originalValue ''. A tuple transform that swaps ['one', 'two'] likewise reports 'one' as the original value of the child that receives 'two'.

findings.claim: The cast path rereads the current item instead of using the element value it already has.
findings.evidence: Array casting already receives the element as v from map, but the helper separately reads parent[k] and originalParent[k]. Tuple casting also rereads the same slot after calling the helper. Capture the item once and reuse that snapshot when the source and processed array are the same.
findings.scenario: Cast an ordinary one-element array with an indexed getter that returns an incrementing number. The baseline read the slot once. The candidate reads it three times and passes value 1 and originalValue 3 to .when() even though the container has no transform.

findings.claim: The regression tests pin exact resolution counts and repeat snapshots that do not distinguish casting from validation.
findings.evidence: The root tests construct separate copies of the same callback to assert exact [0, 1, 0, 1] sequences. The nested tests repeat identical snapshots for unchanged values. Additional correct resolution would fail these tests without violating the task. Reuse a callback and assert the required context on real cast and validation observations, using a coercion to distinguish them where needed.
